why: A call in a `try` body may throw, and the `catch` clause and what follows the `try` then run (doc 'try, catch'): in `use3.m`, `tidy(a)` runs only when `zt(c)` threw after `a = 5`, so it is the root `tidy.m` whatever `return` follows in the body. In `use4.m` the `if` branch returns after `a = 5`, so `tidy(a)` sees only the Gizmo: `Gizmo::tidy`.
